transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
With two days left before the midterm elections, President Trump was campaigning in Kansas
Sunday urging Republicans to show up at the polls.
>> Republicans, we love them.
They're keeping our country -- well, actually, they're making it because we had four years,
which were a disaster.
And we've just made it in two years, what we've done is unprecedented.
America is great again.
America is great again.
>> More than 54 million people have already voted early in this year's midterm elections.
That's according to the University of Florida's election lab, and Paris Tamara Keith has more.
>> This election season started out on favorable ground for Republicans between a Senate map
that runs through red states and all the gerrymandering of House districts.
But voters are unhappy.
The average price of regular gasoline is over $4 a gallon, inflation is up.
People are worried about artificial intelligence and data centers.
The war with Iran is unpopular, and voters are increasingly voicing concerns about corruption.
Senate races in deep red Republican territory are competitive, as are House districts where
President Trump won by 10 points or more just two years ago.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
>> There's renewed optimism that momentum is building toward a new US-Canada trade deal.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says he had a good conversation with President Trump
on trade relations, Dan Karpenshuck reports.
>> Carney posted on X saying the conversation he had with Trump on Saturday builds on what
he called recent constructive discussions on a prospective trade deal.
Carney says a deal would create jobs for Canadian workers, boost affordability for families,
and fully respect Canada's languages, culture, and sovereignty.
He added that Canadian negotiators would be working to deliver that outcome.
For his part, Trump acknowledged that there was a concept of a very good deal for American
farmers, great for the US, and fine for Canada as well.
The trade war with Canada has emerged as deeply unpopular and a major issue for American voters
as the midterms draw near.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenshuck in Toronto.
>> Nine people are dead after a plane crash in South Florida Sunday afternoon, NPR's Chantalice
Duster has the details.
The Learjet 60 crashed in a neighborhood near Crest Haven, Florida, killing everyone on
board, according to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
The FAA says the small plane crashed around 12.50 p.m. local time Sunday.
It had departed Austin-Burkstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas.
The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office closed roads and told people to avoid the area.
It is unknown whether any homes were damaged in the crash.
It is also unclear what caused the crash, and the FAA says it will investigate what
happened.
The National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation.
Chantalice Duster, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
A local cease-fire in the Hairsong region of Ukraine has ended.
The truce had allowed the evacuation of residents in the front-line town of Olesky.
Some 2,000 people were in the town when the truce began, and they were able to choose
evacuation either to Russia or Ukraine.
My Chemical Romance's album "The Black Parade" has now reached the top of the
Billboard album charts, but 20 years after the album was originally released.
That means the album now holds the record for the longest amount of time between release
date and top of the charts, beating out country star Toby Keith, NPR's Andrew Limbong has
more.
>> If you're of a certain age and you've ever stepped foot in a hot topic, here's
something that will perk your ears.
My Chem's "The Black Parade," a concept album about death and grief, came out in 2006
and was a high watermark for the band.
The band is now currently on a huge worldwide tour, celebrating the album complete with
a new 20th anniversary reissue on vinyl CD cassette.
According to Billboard, the album's jump to number one was driven mostly by pure album
sales, as opposed to streaming.
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
>> Miami is held on to the top spot in the AP College football rankings, despite a close
win Saturday against UNC.
Number two Ohio State was replaced by Georgia after the Buckeyes lost to USC.
Utah jumped three spots to third, followed by Notre Dame and UCLA defending champion
Indiana dropped a six, followed by BYU, Kentucky, Alabama, and Texas in tenth.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump campaigns in Kansas urging Republicans to vote two days before midterm elections
Over 54 million people have already voted early in midterms, per University of Florida election lab
Midterm outlook for Republicans weakened by high gas prices, inflation, and unpopular Iran war
Carney says good talk with Trump builds momentum toward new US-Canada trade deal
Nine killed when Learjet 60 crashes in neighborhood near Crest Haven, Florida
Local cease-fire in Ukraine's Hairsong region ends after allowing evacuation of Olesky residents
My Chemical Romance's 'The Black Parade' hits No. 1 on Billboard 20 years after release
Miami holds No. 1 in AP college football rankings after close win over UNC; Georgia tops Ohio State
